chapter: Wider talk: bands, places and players
title: Records he listened to as a young man
summary: He owned King Oliver, Rhythm Kings and Wolverines records and admired Bix.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: That's what it was. Did you listen to records much in New Orleans when you were coming along?

Well, the only, the only, the only, I had a collection of, uh, of all the good records of sports. My, my, my taste was good. Mm-hmm. I had all, all, all, all the, all the Rhythm King records and, and King Oliver records, and stuff like that, see. Mm-hmm. But then my kid brothers got into the goddamn thing and messed them up. Oh, no. Sure. And I had all, I had, uh, two sets of the Wolverines records.

I loved the sound of the way Bix played and everything else, see. Yeah. And, uh, it was, it was just wonderful. You know, Dick Boynard and all the guys and, uh, like I say, I mean, I had a collection of those kind of records. And then sometimes I'd get, uh, like, like Jabril Smith on, or, or some of the Columbia records or the Carriers or something like that, see. Mm-hmm. But, uh, that's the, that's the kind of records that I listen to. Mm-hmm. Um, I didn't have too many Victor records, because Victor at that time, they, they were kind of slow on jazz music, you know what I mean? And, uh, I, I only like my type of, uh, the thing that I like, and that, that kind of playing, and stuff like this. Mm-hmm. I listened to it and tried to enlarge my vocabulary on that stuff, whatever you call it, see.
